title: Accretive Health / A.H. Belo / Apollo Healthcare / Allied Healthcare / AdaptHealth — Accounting Credibility, Asset Monetization and Per-Share Value V9

notes: Raw Short -> actual Long corrections: A.H. Belo 2010, 2012, 2013, 2016, 2017 and Apollo Healthcare 2020.
AHC and AHC. are different historical securities: AHC is A.H. Belo, while AHC. in the source archive is Apollo Healthcare.
No usable source-DB performance rows exist for any Batch 76 idea, so outcomes are evaluated from original thesis terms, filings, cash distributions, corporate actions and operating results.

Accretive Health 2013 failed on its near-term filing/rerating catalyst as accounting restatements led to NYSE suspension and delisting; later R1 RCM strategic value does not retroactively make the original horizon successful.
A.H. Belo 2010-2013 correctly identified monetizable newspaper, real-estate and Classified Ventures assets; 2014 special dividends totaled $3.75/share.

A.H. Belo 2016-2017 still identified real hard assets, but after the earlier major monetizations were gone, print/digital operating decay and long realization duration overwhelmed the remaining SOTP upside.
A.H. Belo executed a 1-for-4 reverse split in 2021 before becoming DallasNews; the 2025 Hearst $16.50/share takeout equals $4.125 on the old pre-split share basis.

Apollo Healthcare's operational turnaround was real, but the actual 2020-12-17 TSX close was C$5.39 and Anjac paid C$4.50 cash/share, a roughly -16.5% price outcome. The original C$14.2 = 260% upside math implicitly used a lower ~C$3.94 reference that did not match the post-date market close.
Allied Healthcare 2009 and 2010 were both successful cash-rich UK homecare longs and ended in Saga's $3.90/share cash acquisition in 2011.

AdaptHealth's 2021 revenue/EBITDA scale-up was real, but the key Luke McGee capital-allocation thesis broke almost immediately; subsequent impairment and weak per-share returns made the security thesis a strong failure.
The obsolete duplicate Apollo canonical without the '_dot_' ticker marker was removed; the wrapper now points to a single Apollo canonical.

batch_lessons: A delayed-filing catalyst should be treated first as an accounting-credibility problem, not merely a temporary disclosure delay.
In declining businesses, hard assets can create strong returns when monetization is near-term and proceeds are actually distributed.
Static cash and real-estate SOTP values need an annual leakage charge for operating losses, pensions, corporate overhead and failed reinvestment.
A.H. Belo's 2012-2013 vintages were superior to its 2016-2017 vintages because realization was closer and liability/time leakage was smaller.
Reverse splits must be reversed when comparing old entry prices with later terminal takeout prices.
A punctuation change in a ticker can represent an entirely different company; AHC and AHC. must not be merged.
A strategic acquisition can validate a turnaround while still disproving an aggressive target multiple.
Cash-rich recurring-service businesses can be excellent strategic-sale candidates when contracts and customer demand are durable.
Roll-up revenue growth is not the same as per-share value growth; acquisition goodwill, leverage and management quality must be evaluated explicitly.
A key-person capital-allocation thesis should be reset immediately when that individual exits, even if near-term company EBITDA still meets plan.
